events.title: Abraham makes his servant swear to find Isaac a wife
events.narrative_summary: Abraham, old and blessed in everything, has his senior servant swear by the God of heaven not to take a Canaanite wife for Isaac but to go to his own land and kindred. The servant asks if he should take Isaac there; Abraham refuses, promises that God's angel will go before him, and releases him from the oath if the woman will not come.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No date is given beyond 'Abraham was old' (v.1). The scene is set after Sarah's burial (Gen 23) and before Isaac's marriage at forty (Gen 25:20). Radak on v.67 says Sarah had been dead three years when Isaac took Rebekah. The journey out (27 d), the stay (1 night) and the journey back (31 d) take about 2.5 months, so the oath falls about 2.75 years after the burial, margin 6 months. Duration about an hour for the speeches.
events.ancient_year_marker: Abraham was old, well advanced in days

events.title: The servant takes ten camels to Nahor's city
events.narrative_summary: The servant takes ten of his master's camels and goods of every kind and sets out for Aram-Naharaim, to the city of Nahor.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The text gives no duration. Hebron to Haran by road is about 869 km; `urim travel --mode donkey` gives 4 km/h, about 32 km a day, elapsed about 27 days. Camels are not a listed mode, so donkey pace is used. Margin 5 days for the route and the identification of Nahor's city. Starts the moment the oath ends.

events.title: The servant kneels his camels at the well outside the city
events.narrative_summary: Outside the city, by the well, the servant makes his camels kneel at evening, the time when the women go out to draw water.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: v.11 says 'at the time of evening, the time of the going out of the women who draw water'. This is the late afternoon draw before dark, set at BEIN_HAARBAYIM (17:30), and the start snaps to the first such time after the journey ends. Margin 30 minutes. Duration is the time to halt and unload.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: At the time of evening, the time the women go out to draw water

events.title: The servant prays for a sign at the well
events.narrative_summary: The servant asks the God of Abraham to grant him success that day, and names the sign: the girl who answers his request for a drink by offering to water his camels too will be the one appointed for Isaac.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Begins when the halt ends, at the same evening. A prayer of three verses takes a few minutes; margin 5 minutes.

events.title: Rebekah comes to the well and waters the servant and his camels
events.narrative_summary: Before the servant has finished speaking, Rebekah, Bethuel's daughter, comes out with her jar. She fills it, gives the servant a drink and then draws water for all his camels while he watches in silence to learn whether the LORD has prospered his journey.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: v.15 'before he had finished speaking' puts her arrival inside the prayer, so the event is anchored on the prayer's START with an offset of 4 minutes (the prayer lasts about 4, so she arrives as it ends; the margin covers 'before he had finished'). Watering ten camels from a well by jar takes about an hour (my estimate). Margin 5 minutes.

events.title: The servant gives Rebekah gold and asks about her family
events.narrative_summary: When the camels have finished drinking, the servant gives Rebekah a gold ring and two gold bracelets and asks whose daughter she is and whether there is room to lodge. She names her father Bethuel and offers straw, fodder and room.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows at once, 'as the camels had finished drinking' (v.22). A short exchange, about ten minutes.
events.ancient_diurnal_marker: When the camels had finished drinking

events.title: The servant bows and blesses the LORD for his guidance
events.narrative_summary: The man bows down and worships the LORD, blessing the God of Abraham who has not abandoned his steadfast love and has led him to his master's kinsmen.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows Rebekah's answer at once, at the well. It overlaps the start of her run home (v.28) and is anchored on the same point; about five minutes.

events.title: Rebekah runs home and tells her mother's house
events.narrative_summary: Rebekah runs to her mother's house and tells them what has happened.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: She leaves as the exchange ends (v.28). The house is in the city, near the well, so about fifteen minutes with the telling.

events.title: Laban runs to the well and brings the servant home
events.narrative_summary: Laban sees the ring and bracelets on his sister and hears her account, then runs out to the man at the well and invites him in. He unloads the camels, gives them straw and fodder, and brings water to wash the feet of the servant and his men.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows Rebekah's report (vv.29-30). Running, greeting, walking in and seeing to the camels and water takes about an hour, still the same evening; margin 15 minutes.

events.title: The servant refuses to eat until he has told his errand
events.narrative_summary: Food is set before him but the servant will not eat until he has spoken. He tells how Abraham was blessed, how Isaac was born to Sarah, the oath he swore, the prayer at the well, Rebekah's answering of it, and how he gave her the gifts, then asks for a plain answer.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the welcome (v.33). The speech retells vv.2-27 and takes about half an hour; margin 15 minutes.

events.title: Laban and Bethuel say the matter comes from the LORD
events.narrative_summary: Laban and Bethuel answer that the matter has come from the LORD and that they cannot say bad or good; Rebekah is before him, to take and go and be the wife of his master's son, as the LORD has spoken.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediate answer to the speech; about ten minutes.

events.title: The servant worships and gives gifts to Rebekah and her family
events.narrative_summary: Hearing their answer, the servant bows to the ground before the LORD. He brings out silver and gold jewelry and garments for Rebekah and gives precious things to her brother and mother.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the consent at once; about twenty minutes.

events.title: The servant and his men eat, drink and stay the night
events.narrative_summary: The servant and the men with him eat and drink and spend the night in Bethuel's house.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The meal follows the gifts; 'they lodged' (v.54) covers the night. The hours until the morning are not timed; four hours is an estimate for the meal and settling down, and the next event snaps to the morning. Margin 1 hour.

events.title: At daybreak the servant asks to be sent to his master
events.narrative_summary: When they rise in the morning the servant asks to be sent back to his master. Rebekah's brother and mother ask that she stay 'days or ten' first, but the servant begs them not to delay him since the LORD has prospered his way.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: v.54 'they rose up in the morning', BOKER (06:00), the first morning after the night event ends. Duration 30 minutes for the exchange. The request for 'days or ten' is only asked, not granted; see the reviewer note on Rashi and Radak.

events.title: Rebekah agrees to go with the man
events.narrative_summary: They decide to call the girl and ask her. They call Rebekah and ask whether she will go with this man, and she says, 'I will go.'
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows at once the same morning; about fifteen minutes.

events.title: Her family blesses Rebekah and sends her off with the servant
events.narrative_summary: They send Rebekah with her nurse, the servant and his men, and bless her that she become thousands of myriads and that her seed possess the gate of those who hate them. Rebekah and her maids mount the camels and follow the man.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The packing and farewell follow the consent; offset 1 hour (my estimate for the preparations), duration 1 hour, margin 1 hour. The same morning.

events.title: The servant takes Rebekah south to Canaan
events.narrative_summary: The servant takes Rebekah and goes his way, back toward his master's land.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No duration is given. Haran to Beer-lahai-roi is about 1015 km by road; `urim travel --mode donkey` gives about 32 km a day, elapsed about 31 days. Margin 5 days. Starts when the departure ends.

events.title: Isaac sees the camels coming and Rebekah veils herself
events.narrative_summary: Isaac, who had come from Beer-lahai-roi and lived in the Negeb, goes out into the field toward evening to meditate and sees camels coming. Rebekah sees him, gets down from her camel, asks the servant who the man is, and covers herself with her veil when she is told it is his master.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: v.63 'at the turning of evening' (Ibn Ezra: close to sunset; Radak: when people go out to walk). The first such time after the journey ends, BEIN_HAARBAYIM (17:30). The text gives only the hour, so margin 30 minutes.

events.title: Isaac marries Rebekah and is comforted after his mother's death
events.narrative_summary: The servant tells Isaac everything he has done. Isaac brings Rebekah into his mother Sarah's tent and takes her as his wife, and loves her, and is comforted after his mother's death.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Follows the meeting the same evening or soon after. The text names no hour; margin 1 day. Radak puts the marriage three years after Sarah died; see the reviewer note comparing it with Gen 25:20 (Isaac forty).

causal_edges.causal_explanation: Having sworn the oath at Abraham's command, the servant sets out for Nahor's city to find Isaac a wife (24:9-10).
Abraham's word that God would send his angel before the servant (24:7) is borne out when the servant is led to the girl at the well, as he confesses in 24:27.
Rebekah's 'I will go' (24:58) is why they send her off with the servant (24:59).
After meeting Rebekah and hearing the servant's report, Isaac takes her into Sarah's tent as his wife (24:66-67).
Laban runs to the man at the well after hearing Rebekah's account and seeing the jewelry on her (24:30).
When the servant presses to go, the family calls Rebekah to ask her own mind (24:57).
The servant asks for the girl who offers to water his camels (24:14), and Rebekah does exactly that (24:18-20).
The servant's account of the oath, the prayer and the sign leads Laban and Bethuel to say the matter is from the LORD (24:50).
